chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abū Jamīlah, from Abū Usāmah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:
A man becomes junub while he does not have any water with him, and he is the Imam of the people. He said: Yes, he performs tayammum and leads them.

key_terms.إِمَامُ: the one leading the congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: performs tayammum as a substitute for wudu (ablution) or ghusl

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah without water perform tayammum and lead others in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who is in the state of janabah and lacks water. It states that such a person may perform tayammum and serve as the Imam leading the people in salat (prayer).
